_: Findings that are open today, each with a reason and the package that closes it. The run is green on today's state and every package takes lines out; a line that stops matching is reported as removable, so this file shrinks instead of growing. Anything no line covers is new and counts. This is the tracker's half of a pair -- the shop has neubau/theme-pruefung/mobil/schwellen.json in the private repo.
_bands: `from` and `to` mean WHOLLY inside that band. A line written for 769 and up does not cover a finding that starts at 320: that would make the ratchet a blanket rather than a line.
_broad_on_purpose: Some lines below cover a whole band on a whole axis rather than naming elements one by one, and that is a decision, not laziness. 'Every fine-pointer overflow between 320 and 440px' is 94 findings across all twelve pages, and they are not 94 decisions: the app has no narrow-window layout at all down there. Ninety-four lines would pretend otherwise, would need editing every time a label changed, and would still all disappear on the same day. The cost is real and stated here: while such a line stands, a NEW overflow inside its band is not flagged. Each one names the package that removes it.
_2026_08_21_static: First run of the automatic stand over index.html's own markup. Two of its three findings were artifacts of measuring without app.js and were fixed in the stand rather than ratcheted: the fourteen settings pills (hidden by body.admin-mode, which app.js:1026 always sets on that page) and #mcp-save-btn (12px because its label comes from the dictionary at runtime).
_2026_08_21_app: First run of --app, and the first time anything measured this app with its own data in it. 152 findings, none of which the static mode could see, because the pages it renders are empty without app.js. The headline is ZOOMED OUT: eleven of the twelve pages are wider than a phone, so the phone shrinks the whole page instead of scrolling it. The dashboard at 320px renders at 53 percent. That is not a table being awkward, it is the entire application at half size on an iPhone SE, and both previous mobile rounds reported green over it.

ratchet.reason: Eleven of twelve pages are wider than the screen below 460px, so the browser widens the LAYOUT viewport instead of scrolling and renders the page zoomed out: dashboard 53% at 320px, calendar 60%, lab 68%, Chargen 70%. `body{overflow-x:hidden}` does not prevent this, which is measured and not assumed -- the widening happened with that rule in place, and hiding the scrollbar is exactly why nobody saw it. The cause is one cause: nothing on these pages is laid out against the space it actually has. P3 gives the boxes container queries so the content fits the box instead of the box being told a width.

The same defect seen from the other axis, and worth keeping as its own line because it looks different: with a MOUSE the browser does not honour the meta viewport, so instead of shrinking the page it lets 94 elements hang past the right edge -- toolbars, filter rows, zone names, the period toggle on the dashboard. Same band, same cause, same package. A narrow desktop window and a phone are the same layout problem wearing two faces, which is rule R1 stated as a measurement.

The bottom navigation's Kalender entry hangs 14px past the right edge at exactly 320px, the narrowest phone still sold. It survives the widened viewport because the bottom bar is fixed and does not scale with it.

Thirteen controls on a desktop are between 13 and 22px tall, under the 24px of WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), level AA: the sort buttons in the Chargen table header, 'Bearb.' and 'Drucken' in Sorten and Labor, 'Wochenrhythmus bearbeiten' at 13px. They are correct under a coarse pointer at every width, because the token layer keys the desktop override on `hover: hover` and coarse devices keep the phone numbers -- half of R1 is already right here. The missing half is that the fine axis has no floor of its own: `--tap` resolves to `auto` there, and 24px is a floor for every pointer, not only for a finger.

Every cell of the month grid is 28px tall under a finger, at every width from 769px up -- a tablet, and a tablet is where a month view gets used standing up. Seven columns of 44px need 308px, so there is room for it at any of these widths; the cells are 28px because the grid sizes its rows by content and nothing floors them. Same package as the line above: the floor follows the pointer.

The collapsible location header in the Chargen list is 21px tall on both axes above 769px. On the coarse axis that is under 44 and on the fine one under 24, so it is the same control failing both floors at once.

The <summary> of #nb-sub-section is 18px tall on a desktop, under WCAG 2.5.8's 24px. Found by the static run before --app existed, and kept as its own line because it is in index.html's markup rather than in anything app.js renders: it is the one finding both modes can see.

_mode: Each line says which MODE can see it. `markup` is the run without --app, over index.html's own markup; `app` is the run with app.js and a seeded database. Without this a line would be reported as 'can go' by whichever mode cannot see it -- the <summary> below is in index.html and is therefore visible to the static run, while in the live app it sits inside a collapsed form and is never measured. A line with no mode belongs to both.
